diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/_trust-script.tpl b/chart/templates/hdlf/_trust-script.tpl
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..538be642
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/_trust-script.tpl
@@ -0,0 +1,335 @@
+{{- define "fl-control-plane.hdlfTrustScript" -}}
+#!/bin/sh
+set -eu
+
+# Preamble: HDLF trust bootstrap and sync flow.
+#
+# This script is rendered into the hdlf-trust Job and the daily trust-sync
+# CronJob. It makes the namespace-local HDLF instance trust the CA issued by
+# cert-manager, then proves that both generated client certificates can use the
+# resulting HDLF WebHDFS endpoint.
+#
+# General flow:
+# 1. Wait until cert-manager, ServiceInstance, and ServiceBinding resources have
+#    produced all secrets and Ready conditions needed for a complete patch.
+# 2. Add data-protection finalizers to the HDLF ServiceInstance and
+#    ServiceBinding so they are not deleted before their trust state is handled.
+# 3. Merge the desired fileContainer trust, reader role, and admin/reader
+#    authorizations into the ServiceInstance parameters without disturbing other
+#    HDLF configuration.
+# 4. Wait until the service broker observes the patched ServiceInstance
+#    generation, which means the trust configuration has been reconciled.
+# 5. Decode the admin and reader certificates plus the ServiceBinding endpoint
+#    data into local files and variables for a live mTLS probe.
+# 6. Call HDLF with each certificate and finish only when both are accepted.
+
+# Helm renders the release-specific resource names, secret names, trust alias,
+# subject patterns, and retry settings into this reusable shell template.
+NAMESPACE={{ .Release.Namespace | quote }}
+SERVICE_INSTANCE={{ printf "%s-hdlf" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}
+SERVICE_BINDING={{ printf "%s-hdlf-binding" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}
+CA_SECRET={{ .Values.hdlf.caSecretName | quote }}
+BINDING_SECRET={{ .Values.hdlf.serviceBinding.secretName | quote }}
+ADMIN_CERT_SECRET={{ .Values.hdlf.clientCertSecretName | quote }}
+READER_CERT_SECRET={{ .Values.hdlf.readerCertSecretName | quote }}
+FINALIZER="fl.sap.com/hdlf-data-protection"
+ALIAS={{ .Values.hdlf.trustAlias | quote }}
+ADMIN_PATTERN={{ printf "CN=%s-hdlf-client" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}
+READER_PATTERN={{ printf "CN=%s-hdlf-reader" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}
+WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS={{ .Values.hdlf.trust.waitTimeoutSeconds | default 900 }}
+RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS={{ .Values.hdlf.trust.reconcileTimeoutSeconds | default 900 }}
+VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS={{ .Values.hdlf.trust.verifyTimeoutSeconds | default 900 }}
+RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS={{ .Values.hdlf.trust.retryIntervalSeconds | default 5 }}
+VERIFY_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS={{ .Values.hdlf.trust.verifyRetryIntervalSeconds | default 10 }}
+ADMIN_CERT_DIR="/tmp/hdlf-admin-cert"
+READER_CERT_DIR="/tmp/hdlf-reader-cert"
+
+# Run a readiness predicate until it succeeds or the timeout is reached.
+wait_until() {
+  description=$1
+  timeout_seconds=$2
+  interval_seconds=$3
+  shift 3
+
+  deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + timeout_seconds ))
+  echo "Waiting for ${description}..."
+  while true; do
+    if "$@"; then
+      echo "${description} ready."
+      return 0
+    fi
+
+    if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
+      echo "Timed out waiting for ${description} after ${timeout_seconds}s." >&2
+      return 1
+    fi
+
+    echo "  not ready, retrying in ${interval_seconds}s..."
+    sleep "$interval_seconds"
+  done
+}
+
+# Read one base64-encoded data entry from a Kubernetes Secret.
+get_secret_data() {
+  secret_name=$1
+  key=$2
+
+  kubectl get secret "$secret_name" -n "$NAMESPACE" -o json 2>/dev/null \
+    | jq -r --arg key "$key" '.data[$key] // ""' 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+# Report whether a Secret key has been populated yet.
+secret_key_ready() {
+  secret_name=$1
+  key=$2
+
+  [ -n "$(get_secret_data "$secret_name" "$key")" ]
+}
+
+# Wait for a Secret key written by cert-manager or the ServiceBinding controller.
+wait_for_secret_key() {
+  secret_name=$1
+  key=$2
+
+  wait_until "Secret ${secret_name}/${key}" \
+    "$WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS" \
+    "$RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS" \
+    secret_key_ready "$secret_name" "$key"
+}
+
+# Report whether a broker-managed Kubernetes resource is Ready.
+resource_ready() {
+  resource_kind=$1
+  resource_name=$2
+
+  kubectl get "$resource_kind" "$resource_name" -n "$NAMESPACE" -o json 2>/dev/null \
+    | jq -e '.status.conditions[]? | select(.type == "Ready" and .status == "True")' \
+    >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+
+# Wait for ServiceInstance or ServiceBinding reconciliation to reach Ready=True.
+wait_for_ready_resource() {
+  resource_kind=$1
+  resource_name=$2
+
+  wait_until "${resource_kind} ${resource_name} Ready condition" \
+    "$WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS" \
+    "$RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS" \
+    resource_ready "$resource_kind" "$resource_name"
+}
+
+# Decode a required Secret key and fail loudly if the key is absent.
+decode_secret_key() {
+  secret_name=$1
+  key=$2
+  encoded_value=$(get_secret_data "$secret_name" "$key")
+  if [ -z "$encoded_value" ]; then
+    echo "Secret ${secret_name}/${key} is empty or missing." >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  printf '%s' "$encoded_value" | base64 -d
+}
+
+# Materialize a Kubernetes TLS Secret as curl-compatible certificate files.
+write_tls_secret() {
+  secret_name=$1
+  target_dir=$2
+
+  mkdir -p "$target_dir"
+  decode_secret_key "$secret_name" "tls.crt" > "${target_dir}/client.crt"
+  decode_secret_key "$secret_name" "tls.key" > "${target_dir}/client.key"
+  chmod 0600 "${target_dir}/client.crt" "${target_dir}/client.key"
+}
+
+# Keep HDLF broker resources protected while they carry managed trust state.
+ensure_finalizer() {
+  resource=$1
+
+  has_finalizer=$(kubectl get "$resource" -n "$NAMESPACE" -o json \
+    | jq -r --arg finalizer "$FINALIZER" \
+      '[.metadata.finalizers[]? | select(. == $finalizer)] | length')
+
+  if [ "$has_finalizer" != "0" ]; then
+    echo "Finalizer already set on ${resource}."
+    return 0
+  fi
+
+  echo "Adding data-protection finalizer to ${resource}..."
+  patch=$(kubectl get "$resource" -n "$NAMESPACE" -o json \
+    | jq -c --arg finalizer "$FINALIZER" \
+      '{metadata: {finalizers: ((.metadata.finalizers // []) + [$finalizer] | unique)}}')
+  kubectl patch "$resource" -n "$NAMESPACE" --type=merge -p "$patch"
+}
+
+# Fetch the current ServiceInstance parameters, defaulting the HDLF subtree.
+current_params() {
+  kubectl get serviceinstance "$SERVICE_INSTANCE" -n "$NAMESPACE" -o json \
+    | jq -c '.spec.parameters // {"data": {"fileContainer": {}}}'
+}
+
+# Build the desired ServiceInstance parameters by replacing only the managed
+# trust alias, reader role, and admin/reader authorization entries.
+desired_params() {
+  params=$1
+  ca_crt=$2
+
+  jq -c -n \
+    --argjson params "$params" \
+    --arg ca_crt "$ca_crt" \
+    --arg alias "$ALIAS" \
+    --arg admin_pattern "$ADMIN_PATTERN" \
+    --arg reader_pattern "$READER_PATTERN" \
+    '$params
+      | .data = (.data // {})
+      | .data.fileContainer = (.data.fileContainer // {})
+      | .data.fileContainer.trusts =
+        ((.data.fileContainer.trusts // [])
+          | map(select(.alias != $alias))
+          + [{alias: $alias, certData: $ca_crt}])
+      | .data.fileContainer.roles =
+        ((.data.fileContainer.roles // [])
+          | map(select(.name != "reader"))
+          + [{name: "reader", privileges: ["browse", "open"]}])
+      | .data.fileContainer.authorizations =
+        ((.data.fileContainer.authorizations // [])
+          | map(select(.pattern != $admin_pattern and .pattern != $reader_pattern))
+          + [
+              {pattern: $admin_pattern,  rank: 1, roles: ["admin"],  trustBindings: [$alias]},
+              {pattern: $reader_pattern, rank: 2, roles: ["reader"], trustBindings: [$alias]}
+            ])'
+}
+
+# Normalize the fileContainer subtree so the script can detect real drift.
+file_container() {
+  params=$1
+  printf '%s' "$params" | jq -S -c '.data.fileContainer // {}'
+}
+
+# Report whether the service broker has observed the latest ServiceInstance spec.
+observed_generation_matches() {
+  expected_generation=$1
+  observed_generation=$(kubectl get serviceinstance "$SERVICE_INSTANCE" -n "$NAMESPACE" \
+    -o jsonpath='{.status.observedGeneration}' 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+  [ "$observed_generation" = "$expected_generation" ]
+}
+
+# Wait for the broker to apply the patched fileContainer configuration.
+wait_for_broker_reconcile() {
+  generation=$(kubectl get serviceinstance "$SERVICE_INSTANCE" -n "$NAMESPACE" \
+    -o jsonpath='{.metadata.generation}')
+
+  wait_until "broker reconciliation for ServiceInstance generation ${generation}" \
+    "$RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS" \
+    "$RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS" \
+    observed_generation_matches "$generation"
+}
+
+# Patch HDLF trust configuration only when the desired fileContainer state differs.
+reconcile_file_container() {
+  ca_crt=$(decode_secret_key "$CA_SECRET" "ca.crt")
+  before_params=$(current_params)
+  after_params=$(desired_params "$before_params" "$ca_crt")
+
+  if [ "$(file_container "$before_params")" = "$(file_container "$after_params")" ]; then
+    echo "HDLF fileContainer trust, roles, and authorizations already match."
+  else
+    echo "Patching HDLF fileContainer trust, roles, and authorizations..."
+    patch=$(jq -c -n --argjson params "$after_params" '{spec: {parameters: $params}}')
+    kubectl patch serviceinstance "$SERVICE_INSTANCE" -n "$NAMESPACE" --type=merge -p "$patch"
+  fi
+
+  wait_for_broker_reconcile
+}
+
+# Load the HDLF hostname and container ID from the ServiceBinding Secret.
+load_binding_credentials() {
+  HDLF_HOST=$(decode_secret_key "$BINDING_SECRET" "files" \
+    | jq -r '.host // empty')
+  CONTAINER_ID=$(decode_secret_key "$BINDING_SECRET" "instance_guid")
+
+  if [ -z "$HDLF_HOST" ] || [ -z "$CONTAINER_ID" ]; then
+    echo "ServiceBinding secret ${BINDING_SECRET} is missing HDLF host or container ID." >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+}
+
+# Probe the HDLF WebHDFS endpoint with one client certificate.
+hdlf_accepts_cert() {
+  cert_path=$1
+  key_path=$2
+
+  http_code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
+    --connect-timeout 10 \
+    --max-time 30 \
+    --cert "$cert_path" \
+    --key "$key_path" \
+    -H "X-SAP-FileContainer: ${CONTAINER_ID}" \
+    "https://${HDLF_HOST}/webhdfs/v1/?op=LISTSTATUS" 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+  [ "$http_code" = "200" ]
+}
+
+# Retry the live mTLS probe until HDLF accepts the certificate.
+verify_hdlf_access() {
+  label=$1
+  cert_path=$2
+  key_path=$3
+
+  wait_until "HDLF to accept the ${label} certificate" \
+    "$VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS" \
+    "$VERIFY_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS" \
+    hdlf_accepts_cert "$cert_path" "$key_path"
+}
+
+# Shared dependency gate used by both init containers and the main patch command.
+wait_for_dependencies() {
+  wait_for_secret_key "$CA_SECRET" "ca.crt"
+  wait_for_secret_key "$ADMIN_CERT_SECRET" "tls.crt"
+  wait_for_secret_key "$ADMIN_CERT_SECRET" "tls.key"
+  wait_for_secret_key "$READER_CERT_SECRET" "tls.crt"
+  wait_for_secret_key "$READER_CERT_SECRET" "tls.key"
+  wait_for_ready_resource "servicebinding" "$SERVICE_BINDING"
+  wait_for_ready_resource "serviceinstance" "$SERVICE_INSTANCE"
+  wait_for_secret_key "$BINDING_SECRET" "files"
+  wait_for_secret_key "$BINDING_SECRET" "instance_guid"
+}
+
+# Orchestrate the full trust sync from Kubernetes prerequisites to live HDLF access.
+patch_trust() {
+  # Step 1: make sure every external controller has produced the inputs we need.
+  wait_for_dependencies
+
+  # Step 2: protect broker resources before mutating trust-related parameters.
+  ensure_finalizer "serviceinstances/${SERVICE_INSTANCE}"
+  ensure_finalizer "servicebindings/${SERVICE_BINDING}"
+
+  # Step 3: converge ServiceInstance fileContainer trust and authorizations.
+  reconcile_file_container
+
+  # Step 4: prepare local certificate files and endpoint data for verification.
+  write_tls_secret "$ADMIN_CERT_SECRET" "$ADMIN_CERT_DIR"
+  write_tls_secret "$READER_CERT_SECRET" "$READER_CERT_DIR"
+  load_binding_credentials
+
+  # Step 5: confirm HDLF accepts both managed identities over mTLS.
+  echo "Verifying HDLF accepts the admin and reader certificates (host=${HDLF_HOST})..."
+  verify_hdlf_access "admin" "${ADMIN_CERT_DIR}/client.crt" "${ADMIN_CERT_DIR}/client.key"
+  verify_hdlf_access "reader" "${READER_CERT_DIR}/client.crt" "${READER_CERT_DIR}/client.key"
+  echo "HDLF trust is live for admin and reader certificates."
+}
+
+case "${1:-patch}" in
+  patch)
+    patch_trust
+    ;;
+  wait-for-dependencies)
+    wait_for_dependencies
+    ;;
+  *)
+    echo "Usage: $0 [patch|wait-for-dependencies]" >&2
+    exit 64
+    ;;
+esac
+{{- end -}}
diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-binding.yaml b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-binding.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..6b01d707
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-binding.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+# Provisions a new HANA Cloud data lake Files-only instance via the BTP
+# operator. One instance per namespace — the operator always creates a fresh
+# instance (adoption of externally-created instances is not supported; see
+# docs/hdlf-service-binding.md).
+#
+# fileContainer is intentionally empty here. The hdlf-trust-job
+# pre-install/pre-upgrade hook patches trusts and authorizations once the
+# cert-manager CA is ready.
+{{- if not (lookup "services.cloud.sap.com/v1" "ServiceInstance" .Release.Namespace (printf "%s-hdlf" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .))) }}
+apiVersion: services.cloud.sap.com/v1
+kind: ServiceInstance
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf
+  finalizers:
+    - fl.sap.com/hdlf-data-protection
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": never
+    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
+spec:
+  externalName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-{{ .Release.Namespace }}
+  serviceOfferingName: hana-cloud
+  servicePlanName: relational-data-lake
+  parameters:
+    data:
+      # Must be explicit: omitting iqEnabled causes the broker to attempt
+      # enabling the Relational Engine, which fails on HDLRE-disabled landscapes.
+      iqEnabled: false
+      fileContainer: {}
+{{- end }}
+---
+# Binds the ServiceInstance and materialises a Kubernetes Secret with the HDLF
+# endpoint credentials (files.host, files.port, instance_guid).
+{{- if not (lookup "services.cloud.sap.com/v1" "ServiceBinding" .Release.Namespace (printf "%s-hdlf-binding" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .))) }}
+apiVersion: services.cloud.sap.com/v1
+kind: ServiceBinding
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-binding
+  finalizers:
+    - fl.sap.com/hdlf-data-protection
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": never
+    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
+spec:
+  serviceInstanceName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf
+  externalName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-binding-{{ .Release.Namespace }}
+  secretName: {{ required "hdlf.serviceBinding.secretName must be set" .Values.hdlf.serviceBinding.secretName }}
+{{- end }}
diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-certs.yaml b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-certs.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..ca04f9a5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-certs.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,119 @@
+# cert-manager resources are pre-hooks because the HDLF trust Job is also a
+# pre-hook and must mount the issued client certificate before application pods
+# roll. Each object is guarded with lookup so upgrades keep existing certs and
+# do not rotate the namespace CA unnecessarily.
+{{- if not (lookup "cert-manager.io/v1" "Issuer" .Release.Namespace (printf "%s-hdlf-selfsigned" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .))) }}
+# Self-signed CA — one per namespace. The CA cert is stored in
+# hdlf.caSecretName and patched into the ServiceInstance fileContainer.trusts
+# by the hdlf-trust-job pre-install/pre-upgrade hook.
+apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
+kind: Issuer
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-selfsigned
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": never
+    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
+spec:
+  selfSigned: {}
+---
+{{- end }}
+{{- if not (lookup "cert-manager.io/v1" "Certificate" .Release.Namespace (printf "%s-hdlf-ca" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .))) }}
+apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
+kind: Certificate
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-ca
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": never
+    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
+spec:
+  isCA: true
+  commonName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-ca
+  secretName: {{ .Values.hdlf.caSecretName }}
+  # CA lives 3 years and renews 7 days before expiry. Client certs live 3 months,
+  # so the CA outlives several client cert rotations. When the CA does rotate,
+  # the hdlf-trust-sync CronJob reconciles the new CA into fileContainer.trusts.
+  duration: 26280h  # 3 years
+  # 7-day overlap window: cert-manager issues the new CA while the old one is
+  # still valid. The daily trust-sync CronJob will detect the change and
+  # register the new CA in HDLF within 24h — well inside the 7-day window.
+  renewBefore: 168h
+  privateKey:
+    algorithm: RSA
+    size: 4096
+  issuerRef:
+    name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-selfsigned
+    kind: Issuer
+    group: cert-manager.io
+---
+{{- end }}
+{{- if not (lookup "cert-manager.io/v1" "Issuer" .Release.Namespace (include "fl-control-plane.hdlfCaIssuerName" .)) }}
+# CA-backed issuer — signs the client certificate below.
+apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
+kind: Issuer
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.hdlfCaIssuerName" . }}
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": never
+    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
+spec:
+  ca:
+    secretName: {{ .Values.hdlf.caSecretName }}
+---
+{{- end }}
+{{- if not (lookup "cert-manager.io/v1" "Certificate" .Release.Namespace (printf "%s-hdlf-client" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .))) }}
+# Client certificate used by the application to authenticate against HDLF.
+apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
+kind: Certificate
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-client
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": never
+    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
+spec:
+  commonName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-client
+  secretName: {{ .Values.hdlf.clientCertSecretName }}
+  duration: 2160h   # 3 months
+  renewBefore: 72h  # 3 days overlap — cert-manager issues new client cert while old is still valid
+  privateKey:
+    algorithm: RSA
+    size: 4096
+  issuerRef:
+    name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.hdlfCaIssuerName" . }}
+    kind: Issuer
+    group: cert-manager.io
+---
+{{- end }}
+{{- if not (lookup "cert-manager.io/v1" "Certificate" .Release.Namespace (printf "%s-hdlf-reader" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .))) }}
+# Read-only client certificate — browse + open only, no write access.
+# Used by components that need to read inspection data but must not modify it.
+# Same lifecycle as the admin client cert (3 months, 3-day renewal overlap).
+apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
+kind: Certificate
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-reader
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": never
+    "helm.sh/resource-policy": keep
+spec:
+  commonName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-reader
+  secretName: {{ .Values.hdlf.readerCertSecretName }}
+  duration: 2160h
+  renewBefore: 72h
+  privateKey:
+    algorithm: RSA
+    size: 4096
+  issuerRef:
+    name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.hdlfCaIssuerName" . }}
+    kind: Issuer
+    group: cert-manager.io
+{{- end }}
diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-hook-rbac.yaml b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-hook-rbac.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..4663354c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-hook-rbac.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,53 @@
+# Hook-scoped RBAC for the pre-install/pre-upgrade trust Job. The daily
+# CronJob uses separately managed RBAC in hdlf-trust-sync-rbac.yaml.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: ServiceAccount
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation
+---
+apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
+kind: Role
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation
+rules:
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["secrets"]
+    resourceNames:
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.caSecretName | quote }}
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.serviceBinding.secretName | quote }}
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.clientCertSecretName | quote }}
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.readerCertSecretName | quote }}
+    verbs: ["get"]
+  - apiGroups: ["services.cloud.sap.com"]
+    resources: ["serviceinstances"]
+    resourceNames: [{{ printf "%s-hdlf" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}]
+    verbs: ["get", "patch"]
+  - apiGroups: ["services.cloud.sap.com"]
+    resources: ["servicebindings"]
+    resourceNames: [{{ printf "%s-hdlf-binding" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}]
+    verbs: ["get", "patch"]
+---
+apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
+kind: RoleBinding
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation
+roleRef:
+  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
+  kind: Role
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust
+subjects:
+  - kind: ServiceAccount
+    name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust
+    namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-hook-script.yaml b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-hook-script.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..ed12e9c4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-hook-script.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+# Hook-scoped copy of the trust script used by the pre-install/pre-upgrade Job.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: ConfigMap
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-script
+  annotations:
+    "helm.sh/hook": pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "3"
+    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": before-hook-creation
+data:
+  patch-trust.sh: |
+{{ include "fl-control-plane.hdlfTrustScript" . | indent 4 }}
diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-job.yaml b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-job.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..e788193d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-job.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+# Pre-install/upgrade Job that wires the cert-manager CA into the HDLF
+# ServiceInstance before the control plane and hdlf-server start.
+#
+# Hook order:
+#   -2  HANA ServiceInstance
+#    1  HANA ServiceBinding
+#    2  db-migrate
+#    3  HDLF ServiceInstance + ServiceBinding + cert-manager Issuers/Certificates
+#       + trust hook RBAC/ConfigMap
+#    4  this Job
+#
+# The mounted script performs bounded waits for async dependencies, applies the
+# desired fileContainer trust state, and verifies both admin and reader certs.
+apiVersion: batch/v1
+kind: Job
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-job
+  annotations:
+    helm.sh/hook: pre-install,pre-upgrade
+    helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation
+    helm.sh/hook-weight: "4"
+spec:
+  backoffLimit: {{ .Values.hdlf.trust.backoffLimit | default 3 }}
+  activeDeadlineSeconds: {{ .Values.hdlf.trust.jobActiveDeadlineSeconds | default 1800 }}
+  template:
+    spec:
+      serviceAccountName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust
+      restartPolicy: OnFailure
+      containers:
+        - name: patch-trust
+          image: alpine/k8s:1.35.4
+          command: ["/bin/sh", "/scripts/patch-trust.sh"]
+          volumeMounts:
+            - name: scripts
+              mountPath: /scripts
+      volumes:
+        - name: scripts
+          configMap:
+            name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-script
+            defaultMode: 0755
diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-sync-cronjob.yaml b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-sync-cronjob.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..7cad0aaa
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-sync-cronjob.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+# Daily reconciliation for CA rotation or accidental HDLF trust drift.
+apiVersion: batch/v1
+kind: CronJob
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync
+spec:
+  # Daily at 03:17 UTC, away from common :00/:30 scheduling spikes.
+  schedule: "17 3 * * *"
+  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
+  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
+  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
+  jobTemplate:
+    spec:
+      backoffLimit: {{ .Values.hdlf.trust.backoffLimit | default 3 }}
+      activeDeadlineSeconds: {{ .Values.hdlf.trust.syncActiveDeadlineSeconds | default 1800 }}
+      template:
+        spec:
+          serviceAccountName: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync
+          restartPolicy: OnFailure
+          containers:
+            - name: patch-trust
+              image: alpine/k8s:1.35.4
+              command: ["/bin/sh", "/scripts/patch-trust.sh"]
+              volumeMounts:
+                - name: scripts
+                  mountPath: /scripts
+          volumes:
+            - name: scripts
+              configMap:
+                name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync-script
+                defaultMode: 0755
diff --git a/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-sync-rbac.yaml b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-sync-rbac.yaml
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..e5c67bcb
--- /dev/null
+++ b/chart/templates/hdlf/hdlf-trust-sync-rbac.yaml
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+# Normal Helm-managed resources for the daily trust-sync CronJob.
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: ServiceAccount
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync
+---
+apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
+kind: Role
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync
+rules:
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["secrets"]
+    resourceNames:
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.caSecretName | quote }}
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.serviceBinding.secretName | quote }}
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.clientCertSecretName | quote }}
+      - {{ .Values.hdlf.readerCertSecretName | quote }}
+    verbs: ["get"]
+  - apiGroups: ["services.cloud.sap.com"]
+    resources: ["serviceinstances"]
+    resourceNames: [{{ printf "%s-hdlf" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}]
+    verbs: ["get", "patch"]
+  - apiGroups: ["services.cloud.sap.com"]
+    resources: ["servicebindings"]
+    resourceNames: [{{ printf "%s-hdlf-binding" (include "fl-control-plane.fullname" .) | quote }}]
+    verbs: ["get", "patch"]
+---
+apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
+kind: RoleBinding
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync
+roleRef:
+  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
+  kind: Role
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync
+subjects:
+  - kind: ServiceAccount
+    name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync
+    namespace: {{ .Release.Namespace }}
+---
+apiVersion: v1
+kind: ConfigMap
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "fl-control-plane.fullname" . }}-hdlf-trust-sync-script
+data:
+  patch-trust.sh: |
+{{ include "fl-control-plane.hdlfTrustScript" . | indent 4 }}
diff --git a/chart/values.yaml b/chart/values.yaml
index e05ab43e..ce882c39 100644
--- a/chart/values.yaml
+++ b/chart/values.yaml
@@ -45,12 +45,6 @@ dbMigrateJob:
       cpu: 500m
       memory: 500Mi
 
-hdlf:
-  restApiHost: "c072e62e-3bdd-445d-9e90-98fc5375bee8.files.hdl.cc.hc-eu01can.hanacloud.ondemand.com"
-  containerId: "c072e62e-3bdd-445d-9e90-98fc5375bee8"

+---
+# Source: cert-manager/templates/crd-acme.cert-manager.io_challenges.yaml
+apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
+kind: CustomResourceDefinition
+metadata:
+  name: "challenges.acme.cert-manager.io"
+  annotations:
+    helm.sh/resource-policy: keep

+    app: "cert-manager"

+    app.kubernetes.io/component: "crds"
+    app.kubernetes.io/version: "v1.20.2"
+spec:
+  group: acme.cert-manager.io
+  names:
+    categories:
+      - cert-manager
+      - cert-manager-acme
+    kind: Challenge
+    listKind: ChallengeList
+    plural: challenges
+    singular: challenge
+  scope: Namespaced
+  versions:
+    - additionalPrinterColumns:
+        - jsonPath: .status.state
+          name: State
+          type: string
+        - jsonPath: .spec.dnsName
+          name: Domain

+        - jsonPath: .status.reason
+          name: Reason
+          priority: 1
+          type: string
+        - description: CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is not guaranteed to be set in happens-before order across separate operations. Clients may not set this value. It is represented in RFC3339 form and is in UTC.
+          jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp
+          name: Age
+          type: date
+      name: v1
+      schema:
+        openAPIV3Schema:
+          description: Challenge is a type to represent a Challenge request with an ACME server
+          properties:
+            apiVersion:
+              description: |-
+                APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
+                Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
+                may reject unrecognized values.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources
+              type: string
+            kind:
+              description: |-
+                Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
+                Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
+                Cannot be updated.
+                In CamelCase.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
+              type: string
+            metadata:
+              type: object
+            spec:
+              properties:
+                authorizationURL:
+                  description: |-
+                    The URL to the ACME Authorization resource that this
+                    challenge is a part of.
+                  type: string
+                dnsName:
+                  description: |-
+                    dnsName is the identifier that this challenge is for, e.g., example.com.
+                    If the requested DNSName is a 'wildcard', this field MUST be set to the
+                    non-wildcard domain, e.g., for `*.example.com`, it must be `example.com`.
+                  type: string
+                issuerRef:
+                  description: |-
+                    References a properly configured ACME-type Issuer which should
+                    be used to create this Challenge.
+                    If the Issuer does not exist, processing will be retried.
+                    If the Issuer is not an 'ACME' Issuer, an error will be returned and the
+                    Challenge will be marked as failed.
+                  properties:
+                    group:
+                      description: |-
+                        Group of the issuer being referred to.
+                        Defaults to 'cert-manager.io'.
+                      type: string
+                    kind:
+                      description: |-
+                        Kind of the issuer being referred to.
+                        Defaults to 'Issuer'.
+                      type: string
+                    name:
+                      description: Name of the issuer being referred to.
+                      type: string
+                  required:
+                    - name
+                  type: object
+                key:
+                  description: |-
+                    The ACME challenge key for this challenge
+                    For HTTP01 challenges, this is the value that must be responded with to
+                    complete the HTTP01 challenge in the format:
+                    `<private key JWK thumbprint>.<key from acme server for challenge>`.
+                    For DNS01 challenges, this is the base64 encoded SHA256 sum of the
+                    `<private key JWK thumbprint>.<key from acme server for challenge>`
+                    text that must be set as the TXT record content.
+                  type: string
+                solver:
+                  description: |-
+                    Contains the domain solving configuration that should be used to
+                    solve this challenge resource.
+                  properties:
+                    dns01:
+                      description: |-
+                        Configures cert-manager to attempt to complete authorizations by
+                        performing the DNS01 challenge flow.
+                      properties:
+                        acmeDNS:
+                          description: |-
+                            Use the 'ACME DNS' (https://github.com/joohoi/acme-dns) API to manage
+                            DNS01 challenge records.
+                          properties:
+                            accountSecretRef:
+                              description: |-
+                                A reference to a specific 'key' within a Secret resource.
+                                In some instances, `key` is a required field.
+                              properties:
+                                key:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                    Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be
+                                    required.
+                                  type: string
+                                name:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                    More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                                  type: string
+                              required:
+                                - name
+                              type: object
+                            host:
+                              type: string
+                          required:
+                            - accountSecretRef
+                            - host
+                          type: object
+                        akamai:
+                          description: Use the Akamai DNS zone management API to manage DNS01 challenge records.
+                          properties:
+                            accessTokenSecretRef:
+                              description: |-
+                                A reference to a specific 'key' within a Secret resource.
+                                In some instances, `key` is a required field.
+                              properties:
+                                key:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                    Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be

+                              required:

+                            clientSecretSecretRef:

+                              properties:

+                                  description: |-

+                              required:

+                              properties:

+                                  description: |-
+                                    The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                    Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be

+                                name:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                    More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                                  type: string
+                              required:
+                                - name
+                              type: object
+                            serviceConsumerDomain:
+                              type: string
+                          required:
+                            - accessTokenSecretRef
+                            - clientSecretSecretRef
+                            - clientTokenSecretRef
+                            - serviceConsumerDomain
+                          type: object
+                        azureDNS:
+                          description: Use the Microsoft Azure DNS API to manage DNS01 challenge records.
+                          properties:
+                            clientID:
+                              description: |-
+                                Auth: Azure Service Principal:
+                                The ClientID of the Azure Service Principal used to authenticate with Azure DNS.
+                                If set, ClientSecret and TenantID must also be set.
+                              type: string
+                            clientSecretSecretRef:
+                              description: |-
+                                Auth: Azure Service Principal:
+                                A reference to a Secret containing the password associated with the Service Principal.
+                                If set, ClientID and TenantID must also be set.
+                              properties:
+                                key:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                    Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be
+                                    required.
+                                  type: string
+                                name:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                    More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                                  type: string
+                              required:
+                                - name
+                              type: object
+                            environment:
+                              description: name of the Azure environment (default AzurePublicCloud)
+                              enum:
+                                - AzurePublicCloud
+                                - AzureChinaCloud
+                                - AzureGermanCloud
+                                - AzureUSGovernmentCloud
+                              type: string
+                            hostedZoneName:
+                              description: name of the DNS zone that should be used
+                              type: string
+                            managedIdentity:
+                              description: |-
+                                Auth: Azure Workload Identity or Azure Managed Service Identity:
+                                Settings to enable Azure Workload Identity or Azure Managed Service Identity
+                                If set, ClientID, ClientSecret and TenantID must not be set.
+                              properties:
+                                clientID:
+                                  description: client ID of the managed identity, cannot be used at the same time as resourceID
+                                  type: string
+                                resourceID:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    resource ID of the managed identity, cannot be used at the same time as clientID
+                                    Cannot be used for Azure Managed Service Identity
+                                  type: string
+                                tenantID:
+                                  description: tenant ID of the managed identity, cannot be used at the same time as resourceID
+                                  type: string
+                              type: object
+                            resourceGroupName:
+                              description: resource group the DNS zone is located in
+                              type: string
+                            subscriptionID:
+                              description: ID of the Azure subscription
+                              type: string
+                            tenantID:
+                              description: |-
+                                Auth: Azure Service Principal:
+                                The TenantID of the Azure Service Principal used to authenticate with Azure DNS.
+                                If set, ClientID and ClientSecret must also be set.
+                              type: string
+                            zoneType:
+                              description: |-
+                                ZoneType determines which type of Azure DNS zone to use.

+                                Valid values are:

+                              enum:
+                                - AzurePublicZone

+                              type: string
+                          required:

+                          type: object

+                              properties:
+                                key:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                    Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be

+                                name:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    Name of the resource being referred to.

+                                  type: string
+                              required:

+                            email:

+                            to manage DNS01 challenge records.
+                          properties:
+                            nameserver:
+                              description: |-
+                                The IP address or hostname of an authoritative DNS server supporting

+                              type: string
+                            protocol:

+                              enum:

+                                name:
+                                  description: |-
+                                    Name of the resource being referred to.

+                                  type: string

+                                          items:
+                                            type: string

+                                          x-kubernetes-list-type: atomic
+                                        name:

+apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1

+          jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp

+      name: v1
+      schema:
+        openAPIV3Schema:
+          description: |-
+            A ClusterIssuer represents a certificate issuing authority which can be
+            referenced as part of `issuerRef` fields.
+            It is similar to an Issuer, however it is cluster-scoped and therefore can
+            be referenced by resources that exist in *any* namespace, not just the same

+          properties:
+            apiVersion:

+            kind:

+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
+              type: string
+            metadata:
+              type: object
+            spec:
+              description: Desired state of the ClusterIssuer resource.
+              properties:
+                acme:
+                  description: |-
+                    ACME configures this issuer to communicate with a RFC8555 (ACME) server
+                    to obtain signed x509 certificates.
+                  properties:
+                    caBundle:
+                      description: |-
+                        Base64-encoded bundle of PEM CAs which can be used to validate the certificate
+                        chain presented by the ACME server.
+                        Mutually exclusive with SkipTLSVerify; prefer using CABundle to prevent various
+                        kinds of security vulnerabilities.
+                        If CABundle and SkipTLSVerify are unset, the system certificate bundle inside
+                        the container is used to validate the TLS connection.
+                      format: byte
+                      type: string
+                    disableAccountKeyGeneration:
+                      description: |-

+                        If true, the Issuer resource will *not* request a new account but will expect
+                        the account key to be supplied via an existing secret.
+                        If false, the cert-manager system will generate a new ACME account key
+                        for the Issuer.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean
+                    email:
+                      description: |-
+                        Email is the email address to be associated with the ACME account.
+                        This field is optional, but it is strongly recommended to be set.
+                        It will be used to contact you in case of issues with your account or
+                        certificates, including expiry notification emails.
+                        This field may be updated after the account is initially registered.
+                      type: string
+                    enableDurationFeature:
+                      description: |-
+                        Enables requesting a Not After date on certificates that matches the
+                        duration of the certificate. This is not supported by all ACME servers
+                        like Let's Encrypt. If set to true when the ACME server does not support
+                        it, it will create an error on the Order.

+                        external account credentials with the registered ACME account.
+                      properties:
+                        keyAlgorithm:
+                          description: |-
+                            Deprecated: keyAlgorithm field exists for historical compatibility

+                            in golang/x/crypto/acme.
+                          enum:
+                            - HS256
+                            - HS384
+                            - HS512
+                          type: string
+                        keyID:
+                          description: keyID is the ID of the CA key that the External Account is bound to.
+                          type: string
+                        keySecretRef:
+                          description: |-

+                            Secret which holds the symmetric MAC key of the External Account Binding.
+                            The `key` is the index string that is paired with the key data in the
+                            Secret and should not be confused with the key data itself, or indeed with
+                            the External Account Binding keyID above.

+                            encoded data.

+                              type: string
+                            name:
+                              description: |-
+                                Name of the resource being referred to.

+                          required:
+                            - name
+                          type: object
+                      required:
+                        - keyID
+                        - keySecretRef
+                      type: object
+                    preferredChain:
+                      description: |-
+                        PreferredChain is the chain to use if the ACME server outputs multiple.
+                        PreferredChain is no guarantee that this one gets delivered by the ACME
+                        endpoint.
+                        For example, for Let's Encrypt's DST cross-sign you would use:
+                        "DST Root CA X3" or "ISRG Root X1" for the newer Let's Encrypt root CA.
+                        This value picks the first certificate bundle in the combined set of
+                        ACME default and alternative chains that has a root-most certificate with
+                        this value as its issuer's commonname.
+                      maxLength: 64
+                      type: string
+                    privateKeySecretRef:

+                        the named Secret resource.

+                      properties:
+                        key:
+                          description: |-

+                            Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be

+                          type: string
+                        name:
+                          description: |-
+                            Name of the resource being referred to.
+                            More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                          type: string
+                      required:
+                        - name
+                      type: object
+                    profile:
+                      description: |-

+                        Supported profiles are listed by the server's ACME directory URL.
+                      type: string
+                    server:
+                      description: |-

+                        For example, for Let's Encrypt's staging endpoint, you would use:

+                                  The Gateway API is a sig-network community API that models service networking
+                                  in Kubernetes (https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/). The Gateway solver will
+                                  create HTTPRoutes with the specified labels in the same namespace as the challenge.
+                                  This solver is experimental, and fields / behaviour may change in the future.

+                                    description: |-
+                                      Custom labels that will be applied to HTTPRoutes created by cert-manager

+                                      When solving an HTTP-01 challenge, cert-manager creates an HTTPRoute.
+                                      cert-manager needs to know which parentRefs should be used when creating
+                                      the HTTPRoute. Usually, the parentRef references a Gateway. See:
+                                      https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/api-types/httproute/#attaching-to-gateways
+                                    items:
+                                      description: |-
+                                        ParentReference identifies an API object (usually a Gateway) that can be considered
+                                        a parent of this resource (usually a route). There are two kinds of parent resources
+                                        with "Core" support:

+                                        * Gateway (Gateway conformance profile)

+
+                                            Support: Core
+                                          maxLength: 253
+                                          pattern: ^$|^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?)*$
+                                          type: string
+                                        kind:
+                                          default: Gateway
+                                          description: |-

+                                          type: string
+                                        namespace:
+                                          description: |-
+                                            Namespace is the namespace of the referent. When unspecified, this refers
+                                            to the local namespace of the Route.
+
+                                            Note that there are specific rules for ParentRefs which cross namespace
+                                            boundaries. Cross-namespace references are only valid if they are explicitly
+                                            allowed by something in the namespace they are referring to. For example:
+                                            Gateway has the AllowedRoutes field, and ReferenceGrant provides a
+                                            generic way to enable any other kind of cross-namespace reference.
+
+                                            <gateway:experimental:description>
+                                            ParentRefs from a Route to a Service in the same namespace are "producer"
+                                            routes, which apply default routing rules to inbound connections from
+                                            any namespace to the Service.
+
+                                            ParentRefs from a Route to a Service in a different namespace are
+                                            "consumer" routes, and these routing rules are only applied to outbound
+                                            connections originating from the same namespace as the Route, for which

+                                        port:

+                                            differently based on the type of parent resource.

+apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
+kind: CustomResourceDefinition
+metadata:
+  name: "issuers.cert-manager.io"
+  annotations:
+    helm.sh/resource-policy: keep
+  labels:
+    app: "cert-manager"
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: "cert-manager"

+    app.kubernetes.io/version: "v1.20.2"
+spec:
+  group: cert-manager.io
+  names:
+    categories:
+      - cert-manager
+    kind: Issuer
+    listKind: IssuerList
+    plural: issuers
+    shortNames:
+      - iss
+    singular: issuer
+  scope: Namespaced
+  versions:
+    - additionalPrinterColumns:

+          name: Ready

+        - jsonPath: .status.conditions[?(@.type == "Ready")].message
+          name: Status
+          priority: 1
+          type: string
+        - description: CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is not guaranteed to be set in happens-before order across separate operations. Clients may not set this value. It is represented in RFC3339 form and is in UTC.
+          jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp
+          name: Age
+          type: date
+      name: v1
+      schema:
+        openAPIV3Schema:
+          description: |-
+            An Issuer represents a certificate issuing authority which can be
+            referenced as part of `issuerRef` fields.
+            It is scoped to a single namespace and can therefore only be referenced by
+            resources within the same namespace.
+          properties:
+            apiVersion:
+              description: |-
+                APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
+                Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
+                may reject unrecognized values.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources
+              type: string
+            kind:
+              description: |-
+                Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
+                Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
+                Cannot be updated.
+                In CamelCase.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
+              type: string
+            metadata:
+              type: object
+            spec:
+              description: Desired state of the Issuer resource.
+              properties:
+                acme:
+                  description: |-
+                    ACME configures this issuer to communicate with a RFC8555 (ACME) server
+                    to obtain signed x509 certificates.
+                  properties:
+                    caBundle:
+                      description: |-
+                        Base64-encoded bundle of PEM CAs which can be used to validate the certificate
+                        chain presented by the ACME server.
+                        Mutually exclusive with SkipTLSVerify; prefer using CABundle to prevent various
+                        kinds of security vulnerabilities.
+                        If CABundle and SkipTLSVerify are unset, the system certificate bundle inside
+                        the container is used to validate the TLS connection.
+                      format: byte
+                      type: string
+                    disableAccountKeyGeneration:
+                      description: |-
+                        Enables or disables generating a new ACME account key.
+                        If true, the Issuer resource will *not* request a new account but will expect
+                        the account key to be supplied via an existing secret.
+                        If false, the cert-manager system will generate a new ACME account key
+                        for the Issuer.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean
+                    email:
+                      description: |-
+                        Email is the email address to be associated with the ACME account.
+                        This field is optional, but it is strongly recommended to be set.
+                        It will be used to contact you in case of issues with your account or
+                        certificates, including expiry notification emails.
+                        This field may be updated after the account is initially registered.
+                      type: string
+                    enableDurationFeature:
+                      description: |-
+                        Enables requesting a Not After date on certificates that matches the
+                        duration of the certificate. This is not supported by all ACME servers
+                        like Let's Encrypt. If set to true when the ACME server does not support
+                        it, it will create an error on the Order.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean

+                      description: |-

+                        server.

+                        external account credentials with the registered ACME account.
+                      properties:
+                        keyAlgorithm:
+                          description: |-
+                            Deprecated: keyAlgorithm field exists for historical compatibility
+                            reasons and should not be used. The algorithm is now hardcoded to HS256
+                            in golang/x/crypto/acme.
+                          enum:

+                            - HS384
+                            - HS512
+                          type: string
+                        keyID:
+                          description: keyID is the ID of the CA key that the External Account is bound to.
+                          type: string
+                        keySecretRef:
+                          description: |-
+                            keySecretRef is a Secret Key Selector referencing a data item in a Kubernetes
+                            Secret which holds the symmetric MAC key of the External Account Binding.
+                            The `key` is the index string that is paired with the key data in the
+                            Secret and should not be confused with the key data itself, or indeed with
+                            the External Account Binding keyID above.
+                            The secret key stored in the Secret **must** be un-padded, base64 URL
+                            encoded data.
+                          properties:
+                            key:

+                                Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be

+                              type: string
+                            name:
+                              description: |-

+                          required:

+                          type: object
+                      required:

+                      type: object

+                      description: |-

+                        PreferredChain is no guarantee that this one gets delivered by the ACME
+                        endpoint.
+                        For example, for Let's Encrypt's DST cross-sign you would use:
+                        "DST Root CA X3" or "ISRG Root X1" for the newer Let's Encrypt root CA.
+                        This value picks the first certificate bundle in the combined set of
+                        ACME default and alternative chains that has a root-most certificate with
+                        this value as its issuer's commonname.

+                      type: string
+                    privateKeySecretRef:

+                        the named Secret resource.
+                        If `key` is not specified, a default of `tls.key` will be used.
+                      properties:

+                          type: string
+                        name:
+                          description: |-
+                            Name of the resource being referred to.
+                            More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                          type: string
+                      required:
+                        - name
+                      type: object
+                    profile:
+                      description: |-
+                        Profile allows requesting a certificate profile from the ACME server.
+                        Supported profiles are listed by the server's ACME directory URL.
+                      type: string
+                    server:
+                      description: |-
+                        Server is the URL used to access the ACME server's 'directory' endpoint.
+                        For example, for Let's Encrypt's staging endpoint, you would use:
+                        "https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory".
+                        Only ACME v2 endpoints (i.e. RFC 8555) are supported.
+                      type: string
+                    skipTLSVerify:
+                      description: |-
+                        INSECURE: Enables or disables validation of the ACME server TLS certificate.
+                        If true, requests to the ACME server will not have the TLS certificate chain
+                        validated.
+                        Mutually exclusive with CABundle; prefer using CABundle to prevent various
+                        kinds of security vulnerabilities.
+                        Only enable this option in development environments.
+                        If CABundle and SkipTLSVerify are unset, the system certificate bundle inside
+                        the container is used to validate the TLS connection.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean
+                    solvers:
+                      description: |-
+                        Solvers is a list of challenge solvers that will be used to solve
+                        ACME challenges for the matching domains.
+                        Solver configurations must be provided in order to obtain certificates
+                        from an ACME server.
+                        For more information, see: https://cert-manager.io/docs/configuration/acme/
+                      items:
+                        description: |-
+                          An ACMEChallengeSolver describes how to solve ACME challenges for the issuer it is part of.
+                          A selector may be provided to use different solving strategies for different DNS names.
+                          Only one of HTTP01 or DNS01 must be provided.

+                            properties:
+                              acmeDNS:

+                                    properties:

+                                        description: |-

+                                      name:

+# Source: cert-manager/templates/rbac.yaml
+# Challenges controller role
+apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
+kind: ClusterRole
+metadata:
+  name: cert-manager-controller-challenges
+  labels:
+    app: cert-manager
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: cert-manager
+    app.kubernetes.io/instance: cert-manager
+    app.kubernetes.io/component: "controller"
+    app.kubernetes.io/version: "v1.20.2"
+rules:
+  # Use to update challenge resource status
+  - apiGroups: ["acme.cert-manager.io"]
+    resources: ["challenges", "challenges/status"]
+    verbs: ["update", "patch"]
+  # Used to watch challenge resources
+  - apiGroups: ["acme.cert-manager.io"]
+    resources: ["challenges"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
+  # Used to watch challenges, issuer and clusterissuer resources
+  - apiGroups: ["cert-manager.io"]
+    resources: ["issuers", "clusterissuers"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
+  # Need to be able to retrieve ACME account private key to complete challenges
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["secrets"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
+  # Used to create events
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["events"]
+    verbs: ["create", "patch"]
+  # HTTP01 rules
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["pods", "services"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "delete"]
+  - apiGroups: ["networking.k8s.io"]
+    resources: ["ingresses"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "delete", "update"]
+  - apiGroups: ["gateway.networking.k8s.io"]
+    resources: ["httproutes"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "delete", "update"]

+  # new ingress resources.
+  # See: https://github.com/openshift/origin/blob/21f191775636f9acadb44fa42beeb4f75b255532/pkg/route/apiserver/admission/ingress_admission.go#L84-L148
+  - apiGroups: ["route.openshift.io"]
+    resources: ["routes/custom-host"]
+    verbs: ["create"]
+  # We require these rules to support users with the OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement
+  # admission controller enabled:
+  # https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#ownerreferencespermissionenforcement
+  - apiGroups: ["acme.cert-manager.io"]
+    resources: ["challenges/finalizers"]
+    verbs: ["update"]
+  # DNS01 rules (duplicated above)
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["secrets"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]

+apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
+kind: CustomResourceDefinition
+metadata:
+  name: "clusterissuers.cert-manager.io"
+  annotations:
+    helm.sh/resource-policy: keep
+  labels:
+    app: "cert-manager"

+spec:
+  group: cert-manager.io
+  names:
+    categories:
+      - cert-manager
+    kind: ClusterIssuer
+    listKind: ClusterIssuerList
+    plural: clusterissuers
+    shortNames:
+      - ciss
+    singular: clusterissuer
+  scope: Cluster
+  versions:
+    - additionalPrinterColumns:
+        - jsonPath: .status.conditions[?(@.type == "Ready")].status
+          name: Ready
+          type: string
+        - jsonPath: .status.conditions[?(@.type == "Ready")].message
+          name: Status
+          priority: 1
+          type: string
+        - description: CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is not guaranteed to be set in happens-before order across separate operations. Clients may not set this value. It is represented in RFC3339 form and is in UTC.
+          jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp
+          name: Age
+          type: date
+      name: v1
+      schema:
+        openAPIV3Schema:
+          description: |-
+            A ClusterIssuer represents a certificate issuing authority which can be
+            referenced as part of `issuerRef` fields.
+            It is similar to an Issuer, however it is cluster-scoped and therefore can
+            be referenced by resources that exist in *any* namespace, not just the same
+            namespace as the referent.
+          properties:
+            apiVersion:
+              description: |-
+                APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
+                Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
+                may reject unrecognized values.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources
+              type: string
+            kind:
+              description: |-
+                Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
+                Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
+                Cannot be updated.
+                In CamelCase.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
+              type: string
+            metadata:
+              type: object
+            spec:
+              description: Desired state of the ClusterIssuer resource.
+              properties:
+                acme:
+                  description: |-
+                    ACME configures this issuer to communicate with a RFC8555 (ACME) server
+                    to obtain signed x509 certificates.
+                  properties:
+                    caBundle:
+                      description: |-
+                        Base64-encoded bundle of PEM CAs which can be used to validate the certificate
+                        chain presented by the ACME server.
+                        Mutually exclusive with SkipTLSVerify; prefer using CABundle to prevent various
+                        kinds of security vulnerabilities.
+                        If CABundle and SkipTLSVerify are unset, the system certificate bundle inside
+                        the container is used to validate the TLS connection.
+                      format: byte
+                      type: string
+                    disableAccountKeyGeneration:
+                      description: |-
+                        Enables or disables generating a new ACME account key.
+                        If true, the Issuer resource will *not* request a new account but will expect
+                        the account key to be supplied via an existing secret.
+                        If false, the cert-manager system will generate a new ACME account key
+                        for the Issuer.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean
+                    email:
+                      description: |-
+                        Email is the email address to be associated with the ACME account.
+                        This field is optional, but it is strongly recommended to be set.
+                        It will be used to contact you in case of issues with your account or
+                        certificates, including expiry notification emails.
+                        This field may be updated after the account is initially registered.
+                      type: string
+                    enableDurationFeature:
+                      description: |-
+                        Enables requesting a Not After date on certificates that matches the
+                        duration of the certificate. This is not supported by all ACME servers
+                        like Let's Encrypt. If set to true when the ACME server does not support
+                        it, it will create an error on the Order.

+                      type: boolean
+                    externalAccountBinding:
+                      description: |-
+                        ExternalAccountBinding is a reference to a CA external account of the ACME
+                        server.

+                        external account credentials with the registered ACME account.
+                      properties:
+                        keyAlgorithm:
+                          description: |-
+                            Deprecated: keyAlgorithm field exists for historical compatibility
+                            reasons and should not be used. The algorithm is now hardcoded to HS256
+                            in golang/x/crypto/acme.
+                          enum:
+                            - HS256
+                            - HS384
+                            - HS512
+                          type: string
+                        keyID:
+                          description: keyID is the ID of the CA key that the External Account is bound to.
+                          type: string
+                        keySecretRef:
+                          description: |-
+                            keySecretRef is a Secret Key Selector referencing a data item in a Kubernetes
+                            Secret which holds the symmetric MAC key of the External Account Binding.
+                            The `key` is the index string that is paired with the key data in the
+                            Secret and should not be confused with the key data itself, or indeed with
+                            the External Account Binding keyID above.
+                            The secret key stored in the Secret **must** be un-padded, base64 URL
+                            encoded data.
+                          properties:
+                            key:
+                              description: |-
+                                The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be
+                                required.
+                              type: string
+                            name:
+                              description: |-
+                                Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                              type: string
+                          required:
+                            - name
+                          type: object
+                      required:
+                        - keyID
+                        - keySecretRef
+                      type: object
+                    preferredChain:
+                      description: |-
+                        PreferredChain is the chain to use if the ACME server outputs multiple.
+                        PreferredChain is no guarantee that this one gets delivered by the ACME

+                            URL is the base URL for the vedsdk endpoint of the CyberArk Certificate Manager Self-Hosted instance,
+                            for example: "https://tpp.example.com/vedsdk".
+                          type: string
+                      required:
+                        - credentialsRef
+                        - url
+                      type: object
+                    zone:
+                      description: |-
+                        Zone is the Certificate Manager Policy Zone to use for this issuer.
+                        All requests made to the Certificate Manager platform will be restricted by the named
+                        zone policy.
+                        This field is required.
+                      type: string
+                  required:
+                    - zone
+                  type: object
+              type: object
+            status:
+              description: Status of the ClusterIssuer. This is set and managed automatically.
+              properties:
+                acme:
+                  description: |-
+                    ACME specific status options.
+                    This field should only be set if the Issuer is configured to use an ACME
+                    server to issue certificates.
+                  properties:
+                    lastPrivateKeyHash:
+                      description: |-
+                        LastPrivateKeyHash is a hash of the private key associated with the latest
+                        registered ACME account, in order to track changes made to registered account
+                        associated with the Issuer
+                      type: string
+                    lastRegisteredEmail:
+                      description: |-
+                        LastRegisteredEmail is the email associated with the latest registered
+                        ACME account, in order to track changes made to registered account
+                        associated with the  Issuer
+                      type: string
+                    uri:
+                      description: |-
+                        URI is the unique account identifier, which can also be used to retrieve

+                  type: object
+                conditions:
+                  description: |-

+                    description: IssuerCondition contains condition information for an Issuer.
+                    properties:

+                          LastTransitionTime is the timestamp corresponding to the last status

+                        format: date-time
+                        type: string
+                      message:
+                        description: |-
+                          Message is a human readable description of the details of the last

+                        type: integer
+                      reason:

+                        type: string
+                      status:
+                        description: Status of the condition, one of (`True`, `False`, `Unknown`).
+                        enum:

+                          - Unknown
+                        type: string
+                      type:
+                        description: Type of the condition, known values are (`Ready`).
