+# Source: cert-manager/templates/crd-cert-manager.io_issuers.yaml
+apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
+kind: CustomResourceDefinition
+metadata:
+  name: "issuers.cert-manager.io"
+  annotations:
+    helm.sh/resource-policy: keep
+  labels:
+    app: "cert-manager"
+    app.kubernetes.io/name: "cert-manager"
+    app.kubernetes.io/instance: "cert-manager"
+    app.kubernetes.io/component: "crds"
+    app.kubernetes.io/version: "v1.20.2"
+spec:
+  group: cert-manager.io
+  names:
+    categories:
+      - cert-manager
+    kind: Issuer
+    listKind: IssuerList
+    plural: issuers
+    shortNames:
+      - iss
+    singular: issuer
+  scope: Namespaced
+  versions:
+    - additionalPrinterColumns:
+        - jsonPath: .status.conditions[?(@.type == "Ready")].status
+          name: Ready
+          type: string
+        - jsonPath: .status.conditions[?(@.type == "Ready")].message
+          name: Status
+          priority: 1
+          type: string
+        - description: CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is not guaranteed to be set in happens-before order across separate operations. Clients may not set this value. It is represented in RFC3339 form and is in UTC.
+          jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp
+          name: Age
+          type: date
+      name: v1
+      schema:
+        openAPIV3Schema:
+          description: |-
+            An Issuer represents a certificate issuing authority which can be
+            referenced as part of `issuerRef` fields.
+            It is scoped to a single namespace and can therefore only be referenced by
+            resources within the same namespace.
+          properties:
+            apiVersion:
+              description: |-
+                APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
+                Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
+                may reject unrecognized values.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources
+              type: string
+            kind:
+              description: |-
+                Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
+                Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
+                Cannot be updated.
+                In CamelCase.
+                More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
+              type: string
+            metadata:
+              type: object
+            spec:
+              description: Desired state of the Issuer resource.
+              properties:
+                acme:
+                  description: |-
+                    ACME configures this issuer to communicate with a RFC8555 (ACME) server
+                    to obtain signed x509 certificates.
+                  properties:
+                    caBundle:
+                      description: |-
+                        Base64-encoded bundle of PEM CAs which can be used to validate the certificate
+                        chain presented by the ACME server.
+                        Mutually exclusive with SkipTLSVerify; prefer using CABundle to prevent various
+                        kinds of security vulnerabilities.
+                        If CABundle and SkipTLSVerify are unset, the system certificate bundle inside
+                        the container is used to validate the TLS connection.
+                      format: byte
+                      type: string
+                    disableAccountKeyGeneration:
+                      description: |-
+                        Enables or disables generating a new ACME account key.
+                        If true, the Issuer resource will *not* request a new account but will expect
+                        the account key to be supplied via an existing secret.
+                        If false, the cert-manager system will generate a new ACME account key
+                        for the Issuer.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean
+                    email:
+                      description: |-
+                        Email is the email address to be associated with the ACME account.
+                        This field is optional, but it is strongly recommended to be set.
+                        It will be used to contact you in case of issues with your account or
+                        certificates, including expiry notification emails.
+                        This field may be updated after the account is initially registered.
+                      type: string
+                    enableDurationFeature:
+                      description: |-
+                        Enables requesting a Not After date on certificates that matches the
+                        duration of the certificate. This is not supported by all ACME servers
+                        like Let's Encrypt. If set to true when the ACME server does not support
+                        it, it will create an error on the Order.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean
+                    externalAccountBinding:
+                      description: |-
+                        ExternalAccountBinding is a reference to a CA external account of the ACME
+                        server.
+                        If set, upon registration cert-manager will attempt to associate the given
+                        external account credentials with the registered ACME account.
+                      properties:
+                        keyAlgorithm:
+                          description: |-
+                            Deprecated: keyAlgorithm field exists for historical compatibility
+                            reasons and should not be used. The algorithm is now hardcoded to HS256
+                            in golang/x/crypto/acme.
+                          enum:
+                            - HS256
+                            - HS384
+                            - HS512
+                          type: string
+                        keyID:
+                          description: keyID is the ID of the CA key that the External Account is bound to.
+                          type: string
+                        keySecretRef:
+                          description: |-
+                            keySecretRef is a Secret Key Selector referencing a data item in a Kubernetes
+                            Secret which holds the symmetric MAC key of the External Account Binding.
+                            The `key` is the index string that is paired with the key data in the
+                            Secret and should not be confused with the key data itself, or indeed with
+                            the External Account Binding keyID above.
+                            The secret key stored in the Secret **must** be un-padded, base64 URL
+                            encoded data.
+                          properties:
+                            key:
+                              description: |-
+                                The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be
+                                required.
+                              type: string
+                            name:
+                              description: |-
+                                Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                              type: string
+                          required:
+                            - name
+                          type: object
+                      required:
+                        - keyID
+                        - keySecretRef
+                      type: object
+                    preferredChain:
+                      description: |-
+                        PreferredChain is the chain to use if the ACME server outputs multiple.
+                        PreferredChain is no guarantee that this one gets delivered by the ACME
+                        endpoint.
+                        For example, for Let's Encrypt's DST cross-sign you would use:
+                        "DST Root CA X3" or "ISRG Root X1" for the newer Let's Encrypt root CA.
+                        This value picks the first certificate bundle in the combined set of
+                        ACME default and alternative chains that has a root-most certificate with
+                        this value as its issuer's commonname.
+                      maxLength: 64
+                      type: string
+                    privateKeySecretRef:
+                      description: |-
+                        PrivateKey is the name of a Kubernetes Secret resource that will be used to
+                        store the automatically generated ACME account private key.
+                        Optionally, a `key` may be specified to select a specific entry within
+                        the named Secret resource.
+                        If `key` is not specified, a default of `tls.key` will be used.
+                      properties:
+                        key:
+                          description: |-
+                            The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                            Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be
+                            required.
+                          type: string
+                        name:
+                          description: |-
+                            Name of the resource being referred to.
+                            More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                          type: string
+                      required:
+                        - name
+                      type: object
+                    profile:
+                      description: |-
+                        Profile allows requesting a certificate profile from the ACME server.
+                        Supported profiles are listed by the server's ACME directory URL.
+                      type: string
+                    server:
+                      description: |-
+                        Server is the URL used to access the ACME server's 'directory' endpoint.
+                        For example, for Let's Encrypt's staging endpoint, you would use:
+                        "https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory".
+                        Only ACME v2 endpoints (i.e. RFC 8555) are supported.
+                      type: string
+                    skipTLSVerify:
+                      description: |-
+                        INSECURE: Enables or disables validation of the ACME server TLS certificate.
+                        If true, requests to the ACME server will not have the TLS certificate chain
+                        validated.
+                        Mutually exclusive with CABundle; prefer using CABundle to prevent various
+                        kinds of security vulnerabilities.
+                        Only enable this option in development environments.
+                        If CABundle and SkipTLSVerify are unset, the system certificate bundle inside
+                        the container is used to validate the TLS connection.
+                        Defaults to false.
+                      type: boolean
+                    solvers:
+                      description: |-
+                        Solvers is a list of challenge solvers that will be used to solve
+                        ACME challenges for the matching domains.
+                        Solver configurations must be provided in order to obtain certificates
+                        from an ACME server.
+                        For more information, see: https://cert-manager.io/docs/configuration/acme/
+                      items:
+                        description: |-
+                          An ACMEChallengeSolver describes how to solve ACME challenges for the issuer it is part of.
+                          A selector may be provided to use different solving strategies for different DNS names.
+                          Only one of HTTP01 or DNS01 must be provided.
+                        properties:
+                          dns01:
+                            description: |-
+                              Configures cert-manager to attempt to complete authorizations by
+                              performing the DNS01 challenge flow.
+                            properties:
+                              acmeDNS:
+                                description: |-
+                                  Use the 'ACME DNS' (https://github.com/joohoi/acme-dns) API to manage
+                                  DNS01 challenge records.
+                                properties:
+                                  accountSecretRef:
+                                    description: |-
+                                      A reference to a specific 'key' within a Secret resource.
+                                      In some instances, `key` is a required field.
+                                    properties:
+                                      key:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                          Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be
+                                          required.
+                                        type: string
+                                      name:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                          More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                                        type: string
+                                    required:
+                                      - name
+                                    type: object
+                                  host:
+                                    type: string
+                                required:
+                                  - accountSecretRef
+                                  - host
+                                type: object
+                              akamai:
+                                description: Use the Akamai DNS zone management API to manage DNS01 challenge records.

+                                    properties:
+                                      key:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                          Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be
+                                          required.
+                                        type: string
+                                      name:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                          More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                                        type: string
+                                    required:
+                                      - name
+                                    type: object

+                                    description: |-
+                                      A reference to a specific 'key' within a Secret resource.

+                                    properties:
+                                      key:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                          Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be

+                                      name:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          Name of the resource being referred to.

+                                        type: string
+                                    required:
+                                      - name
+                                    type: object
+                                  clientTokenSecretRef:
+                                    description: |-
+                                      A reference to a specific 'key' within a Secret resource.
+                                      In some instances, `key` is a required field.
+                                    properties:
+                                      key:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          The key of the entry in the Secret resource's `data` field to be used.
+                                          Some instances of this field may be defaulted, in others it may be

+                                      name:
+                                        description: |-
+                                          Name of the resource being referred to.
+                                          More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
+                                        type: string
+                                    required:
+                                      - name
+                                    type: object
+                                  serviceConsumerDomain:
+                                    type: string
+                                required:
+                                  - accessTokenSecretRef
+                                  - clientSecretSecretRef
+                                  - clientTokenSecretRef
+                                  - serviceConsumerDomain
+                                type: object
+                              azureDNS:
+                                description: Use the Microsoft Azure DNS API to manage DNS01 challenge records.
+                                properties:
+                                  clientID:
+                                    description: |-
+                                      Auth: Azure Service Principal:
+                                      The ClientID of the Azure Service Principal used to authenticate with Azure DNS.
+                                      If set, ClientSecret and TenantID must also be set.
+                                    type: string
+                                  clientSecretSecretRef:
+                                    description: |-

+                                        type: string
+                                    required:
+                                      - name
+                                    type: object
+                                  environment:
+                                    description: name of the Azure environment (default AzurePublicCloud)
+                                    enum:

+                                      - AzureUSGovernmentCloud

+                                    properties:

+                                        type: string
+                                      resourceID:

+                                          Cannot be used for Azure Managed Service Identity
+                                        type: string
+                                      tenantID:
+                                        description: tenant ID of the managed identity, cannot be used at the same time as resourceID
+                                        type: string
+                                    type: object

+                                    description: resource group the DNS zone is located in
+                                    type: string
+                                  subscriptionID:
+                                    description: ID of the Azure subscription

+                                    type: string

+                                    description: |-
+                                      ZoneType determines which type of Azure DNS zone to use.

+                                      name:

+                                      name:
+                                        description: |-

+                                        type: string
+                                    required:
+                                      - name
+                                    type: object
+                                  email:

+                                    type: string
+                                type: object
+                              cnameStrategy:

+                                  CNAMEStrategy configures how the DNS01 provider should handle CNAME

+                                enum:
+                                  - None

+                                type: string
+                              digitalocean:
+                                description: Use the DigitalOcean DNS API to manage DNS01 challenge records.

+                                      name:

+  - apiGroups: ["acme.cert-manager.io"]

+    verbs: ["update", "patch"]
+  # Used to watch challenge resources

+    resources: ["challenges"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
+  # Used to watch challenges, issuer and clusterissuer resources

+    resources: ["issuers", "clusterissuers"]

+    resources: ["secrets"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
+  # Used to create events
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["events"]
+    verbs: ["create", "patch"]

+    verbs: ["update"]

+    resources: ["secrets"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]

diff --git a/engineering_agent/app/hdlf_server_credentials.py b/engineering_agent/app/hdlf_server_credentials.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..0a901591
--- /dev/null
+++ b/engineering_agent/app/hdlf_server_credentials.py
@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+"""HDLF-server request credential headers."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, SecretStr
+
+HDLF_REST_API_HOST_HEADER = "X-HDLF-REST-API-HOST"
+HDLF_CONTAINER_ID_HEADER = "X-HDLF-CONTAINER-ID"
+HDLF_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_HEADER = "X-HDLF-CLIENT-CERTIFICATE"
+HDLF_CLIENT_KEY_HEADER = "X-HDLF-CLIENT-KEY"
+
+
+def _escape_header_value(value: str) -> str:
+    """Escape multiline env values so they are valid single-line HTTP headers."""
+    normalized = value.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
+    return normalized.replace("\n", "\\n")
+
+
+class HdlfServerCredentials(BaseModel):
+    """Credentials forwarded to hdlf-server for request-scoped HDLF access."""
+
+    rest_api_host: str
+    container_id: str
+    client_certificate: SecretStr
+    client_key: SecretStr
+
+    def to_headers(self) -> dict[str, str]:
+        """Return headers consumed by hdlf_server request dependencies."""
+        return {
+            HDLF_REST_API_HOST_HEADER: self.rest_api_host,
+            HDLF_CONTAINER_ID_HEADER: self.container_id,
+            HDLF_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_HEADER: _escape_header_value(
+                self.client_certificate.get_secret_value()
+            ),
+            HDLF_CLIENT_KEY_HEADER: _escape_header_value(self.client_key.get_secret_value()),
+        }

+    cert = "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\ncert-body\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
+    key = "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nkey-body\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
+    multiline_note = "line one\nline two"
+    local_multiline_note = "local line one\nlocal line two"
+
+    with (
+        patch.dict(
+            os.environ,
+            {
+                "MCP_HDLF_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE": cert,
+                "MCP_HDLF_CLIENT_KEY": key,
+                "MCP_MULTILINE_NOTE": multiline_note,
+                "LOCAL_MULTILINE_NOTE": local_multiline_note,
+            },
+        ),
+        patch("app.agent_task_runner.pipeline3", mock_p3),
+        patch("app.agent_task_runner.scheduling_doit", mock_sd),
+    ):
+        run(req, inspection_id="test-inspection-1")
+        assert os.environ["MCP_HDLF_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE"] == cert.replace("\n", "\\n")
+        assert os.environ["MCP_HDLF_CLIENT_KEY"] == key.replace("\n", "\\n")
+        assert os.environ["MCP_MULTILINE_NOTE"] == multiline_note.replace("\n", "\\n")
+        assert os.environ["LOCAL_MULTILINE_NOTE"] == local_multiline_note
+        mock_sd.schedule_tasks.assert_called_once()
+
+

diff --git a/fl_control_plane/execution_engine/hdlf_cert_provisioner.py b/fl_control_plane/execution_engine/hdlf_cert_provisioner.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..afa0bdfd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/fl_control_plane/execution_engine/hdlf_cert_provisioner.py
@@ -0,0 +1,385 @@
+"""Issue short-lived per-inspection HDLF client certificates via cert-manager."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import base64
+import binascii
+from uuid import uuid4
+
+import structlog
+from kubernetes_asyncio import client
+from pydantic import SecretStr
+from temporalio.exceptions import ApplicationError
+
+from fl_control_plane.execution_engine.config import get_settings
+from fl_shared.hdlf_client import HdlfClient
+from fl_shared.hdlf_client.config import settings as hdlf_settings
+
+log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)
+
+_CERT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 2
+_CERT_POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60
+_INSPECTION_POLICY_PRIVILEGES = ["browse", "open", "create", "append", "rename", "delete"]
+_ACCESS_PROBE_BYTES = b"pipeline-fl-hdlf-access-probe\n"
+
+
+def _cert_name(execution_id: str) -> str:
+    return f"fl-job-{execution_id}-hdlf-cert"
+
+
+async def issue_inspection_cert(
+    inspection_id: str,
+    execution_id: str,
+    issuer_name: str,
+    namespace: str,
+    duration_hours: int = 6,
+) -> str:
+    """Create a cert-manager Certificate CR for one inspection and return its Secret name.
+
+    cert-manager generates the RSA key pair itself, signs the certificate with the
+    per-namespace CA-backed Issuer, and writes both ``tls.crt`` and ``tls.key`` into
+    the Secret named ``fl-job-<execution_id>-hdlf-cert``. No Python crypto operations
+    are needed — all key material is managed by cert-manager.
+
+    The certificate CN is set to ``inspection_id`` so the HDLF policy subject
+    ``x509:CN=<inspection_id>`` matches.
+
+    Args:
+        inspection_id: Inspection UUID. Becomes the certificate CN and the HDLF
+            policy subject.
+        execution_id: Handler execution UUID. Gives the Certificate CR and Secret
+            a name unique per job attempt.
+        issuer_name: Name of the cert-manager Issuer in the same namespace, e.g.
+            ``pipeline-fl-hdlf-ca-issuer``.
+        namespace: Kubernetes namespace where the Certificate CR is created.
+        duration_hours: Requested certificate lifetime in hours.
+
+    Returns:
+        The Secret name that cert-manager will write the certificate into.
+        Reference this name via ``secretKeyRef`` in the job manifest.
+
+    Raises:
+        TimeoutError: If cert-manager does not mark the Certificate Ready within
+            ``_CERT_POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`` seconds.
+        IOError: If cert-manager marks the Certificate as failed.
+    """
+    cert_name = _cert_name(execution_id)
+    secret_name = cert_name
+
+    cert_body = {
+        "apiVersion": "cert-manager.io/v1",
+        "kind": "Certificate",
+        "metadata": {
+            "name": cert_name,
+            "namespace": namespace,
+            "labels": {
+                "fl.sap.com/inspection-id": inspection_id,
+                "fl.sap.com/execution-id": execution_id,
+            },
+        },
+        "spec": {
+            "secretName": secret_name,
+            "commonName": inspection_id,
+            "duration": f"{duration_hours}h",
+            # renewBefore is intentionally absent — this cert is single-use and
+            # will be deleted (with the Job) long before it would expire.
+            "privateKey": {
+                "algorithm": "RSA",
+                "size": 2048,
+            },
+            "issuerRef": {
+                "name": issuer_name,
+                "kind": "Issuer",
+                "group": "cert-manager.io",
+            },
+        },
+    }
+
+    async with client.ApiClient() as api_client:
+        custom = client.CustomObjectsApi(api_client)
+        try:
+            await custom.create_namespaced_custom_object(
+                group="cert-manager.io",
+                version="v1",
+                namespace=namespace,
+                plural="certificates",
+                body=cert_body,
+            )
+            log.info(
+                "Certificate CR created",
+                cert_name=cert_name,
+                inspection_id=inspection_id,
+                duration_hours=duration_hours,
+            )
+        except client.ApiException as exc:
+            if exc.status == 409:
+                # Certificate already exists from a prior attempt whose response
+                # was lost. Treat as success and just poll for Ready.
+                log.info(
+                    "Certificate CR already exists, polling for Ready",
+                    cert_name=cert_name,
+                    inspection_id=inspection_id,
+                )
+            else:
+                raise
+        await _poll_certificate(custom, cert_name, namespace)
+
+    return secret_name
+
+
+async def _poll_certificate(
+    custom: client.CustomObjectsApi,
+    cert_name: str,
+    namespace: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Poll a Certificate CR until cert-manager marks it Ready.
+
+    Args:
+        custom: Already-open CustomObjectsApi instance.
+        cert_name: Name of the Certificate CR.
+        namespace: Namespace the CR lives in.
+
+    Raises:
+        TimeoutError: If Ready condition is not True within the polling window.
+        IOError: If cert-manager sets a non-True Ready condition with a reason.
+    """
+    deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + _CERT_POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
+    while True:
+        cert = await custom.get_namespaced_custom_object(
+            group="cert-manager.io",
+            version="v1",
+            namespace=namespace,
+            plural="certificates",
+            name=cert_name,
+        )
+        conditions = (cert.get("status") or {}).get("conditions") or []
+        for condition in conditions:
+            if condition.get("type") == "Ready":
+                if condition.get("status") == "True":
+                    log.info("Certificate ready", cert_name=cert_name)
+                    return
+                if condition.get("status") == "False":
+                    reason = condition.get("reason", "unknown")
+                    message = condition.get("message", "")
+                    raise IOError(
+                        f"Certificate {cert_name!r} failed: {reason} — {message}"
+                    )
+
+        if asyncio.get_running_loop().time() >= deadline:
+            raise TimeoutError(
+                f"Certificate {cert_name!r} did not become Ready within "
+                f"{_CERT_POLL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s"
+            )
+
+        await asyncio.sleep(_CERT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
+
+
+async def _read_tls_secret(secret_name: str, namespace: str) -> tuple[SecretStr, SecretStr]:
+    """Read a Kubernetes TLS Secret and return PEM certificate/key values.
+
+    Args:
+        secret_name: Secret containing ``tls.crt`` and ``tls.key``.
+        namespace: Kubernetes namespace where the Secret lives.
+
+    Returns:
+        The decoded certificate and private key as SecretStr values.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If either key is missing or cannot be decoded.
+    """
+    async with client.ApiClient() as api_client:
+        secret = await client.CoreV1Api(api_client).read_namespaced_secret(
+            name=secret_name,
+            namespace=namespace,
+        )
+
+    data = secret.data or {}
+    try:
+        cert = base64.b64decode(data["tls.crt"], validate=True).decode()
+        key = base64.b64decode(data["tls.key"], validate=True).decode()
+    except KeyError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"Secret {secret_name!r} is missing {exc.args[0]!r}") from exc
+    except (binascii.Error, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"Secret {secret_name!r} contains non-UTF-8 TLS data") from exc
+
+    return SecretStr(cert), SecretStr(key)
+
+
+async def _poll_hdlf_inspection_access(
+    hdlf_client: HdlfClient,
+    inspection_id: str,
+    identity_label: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Wait until HDLF accepts read/write operations for the inspection folder.
+
+    cert-manager readiness only means Kubernetes has a signed certificate. HDLF
+    policy and trust changes are eventually consistent, so the first WebHDFS
+    calls can briefly return 403 even after all Kubernetes objects are Ready.
+
+    Args:
+        hdlf_client: Open HDLF client using the identity being verified.
+        inspection_id: Inspection UUID whose folder must accept the temp-file probe.
+        identity_label: Human-readable identity for logs/errors.
+
+    Raises:
+        TimeoutError: If HDLF does not accept the identity before the deadline.
+    """
+    settings = get_settings()
+    timeout_seconds = settings.hdlf_access_poll_timeout_seconds
+    interval_seconds = settings.hdlf_access_poll_interval_seconds
+    deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + timeout_seconds
+    last_error: Exception | None = None
+    probe_path = f"{inspection_id}/.fl-access-probe-{uuid4().hex}"
+
+    while True:
+        try:
+            await _probe_hdlf_inspection_access(hdlf_client, probe_path)
+            log.info(
+                "HDLF inspection access ready",
+                inspection_id=inspection_id,
+                identity=identity_label,
+            )
+            return
+        except IOError as exc:
+            last_error = exc
+
+        if asyncio.get_running_loop().time() >= deadline:
+            raise TimeoutError(
+                f"HDLF did not accept {identity_label} access to inspection "
+                f"folder {inspection_id!r} "
+                f"within {timeout_seconds}s; last error: {last_error}"
+            ) from last_error
+
+        log.info(
+            "Waiting for HDLF inspection access",
+            inspection_id=inspection_id,
+            identity=identity_label,
+            last_error=str(last_error),
+        )
+        await asyncio.sleep(interval_seconds)
+
+
+async def _probe_hdlf_inspection_access(hdlf_client: HdlfClient, probe_path: str) -> None:
+    """Verify an identity can create, stat, read, and delete inside an inspection folder."""
+    wrote_probe = False
+    try:
+        await hdlf_client.put_object(probe_path, _ACCESS_PROBE_BYTES, overwrite=True)
+        wrote_probe = True
+        if not await hdlf_client.exists(probe_path):
+            raise IOError(f"HDLF access probe {probe_path!r} was written but GETFILESTATUS did not find it")
+        body = await hdlf_client.get_object(probe_path)
+        if body != _ACCESS_PROBE_BYTES:
+            raise IOError(f"HDLF access probe {probe_path!r} returned different bytes than were written")
+    finally:
+        if wrote_probe:
+            await hdlf_client.delete_object(probe_path)
+
+
+async def patch_certificate_owner(
+    execution_id: str,
+    namespace: str,
+    job_uid: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Set the Job as owner of the Certificate CR so k8s GC cleans it up.
+
+    Called after the Job is created and its UID is known. When the Job is
+    garbage-collected (via ttlSecondsAfterFinished), Kubernetes cascades
+    deletion to the Certificate. If cert-manager is configured with
+    ``--enable-certificate-owner-ref``, it will also delete the Secret.
+
+    Failure is logged but not re-raised — the job runs correctly without the
+    ownerReference; the Certificate (and its Secret) will linger until
+    manual cleanup.
+
+    Args:
+        execution_id: Handler execution UUID — used to locate the Certificate CR.
+        namespace: Kubernetes namespace.
+        job_uid: UID of the created Job.
+    """
+    cert_name = _cert_name(execution_id)
+    owner_ref = [
+        {
+            "apiVersion": "batch/v1",
+            "kind": "Job",
+            "name": f"fl-job-{execution_id}",
+            "uid": job_uid,
+            "blockOwnerDeletion": True,
+            "controller": True,
+        }
+    ]
+    try:
+        async with client.ApiClient() as api_client:
+            await client.CustomObjectsApi(api_client).patch_namespaced_custom_object(
+                group="cert-manager.io",
+                version="v1",
+                namespace=namespace,
+                plural="certificates",
+                name=cert_name,
+                body={"metadata": {"ownerReferences": owner_ref}},
+            )
+        log.info("Certificate owner patched", cert_name=cert_name, job_uid=job_uid)
+    except Exception:
+        log.warning(
+            "Failed to patch ownerReferences on Certificate — it will linger after Job GC",
+            cert_name=cert_name,
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+
+
+async def provision_inspection_access(inspection_id: str, execution_id: str) -> str:
+    """Grant HDLF folder policy and issue a per-inspection client cert for a job.
+
+    Shared by both handler and finalizer job submission. ``EE_HDLF_CA_ISSUER_NAME``
+    must be set because handler and finalizer jobs need a per-inspection HDLF
+    identity to read inputs and write results.
+
+    Args:
+        inspection_id: Inspection UUID. Becomes the policy subject and cert CN.
+        execution_id: Job execution UUID. Names the Certificate CR and Secret.
+
+    Returns:
+        The cert Secret name (``fl-job-<execution_id>-hdlf-cert``).
+
+    Raises:
+        ApplicationError: Non-retryable ``ConfigError`` when the HDLF CA issuer
+            setting is missing.
+    """
+    settings = get_settings()
+    if not settings.hdlf_ca_issuer_name:
+        raise ApplicationError(
+            "EE_HDLF_CA_ISSUER_NAME must be set to issue per-inspection HDLF certificates",
+            type="ConfigError",
+            non_retryable=True,
+        )
+
+    async with HdlfClient(
+        hdlf_settings.hdlf_rest_api_host,
+        hdlf_settings.hdlf_container_id,
+        cert_dir=hdlf_settings.hdlf_cert_dir,
+    ) as admin_client:
+        await admin_client.create_policy(
+            policy_name=f"fl-inspection-{inspection_id}",
+            path=f"/{inspection_id}/",
+            subject_cn=inspection_id,
+            privileges=_INSPECTION_POLICY_PRIVILEGES,
+        )
+        await _poll_hdlf_inspection_access(admin_client, inspection_id, "namespace-admin")
+
+    secret_name = await issue_inspection_cert(
+        inspection_id=inspection_id,
+        execution_id=execution_id,
+        issuer_name=settings.hdlf_ca_issuer_name,
+        namespace=settings.namespace,
+        duration_hours=settings.hdlf_inspection_cert_duration_hours,
+    )
+    cert, key = await _read_tls_secret(secret_name, settings.namespace)
+    async with HdlfClient(
+        hdlf_settings.hdlf_rest_api_host,
+        hdlf_settings.hdlf_container_id,
+        client_certificate=cert,
+        client_key=key,
+    ) as inspection_client:
+        await _poll_hdlf_inspection_access(inspection_client, inspection_id, "per-inspection")
+
+    return secret_name

@@ -659,6 +659,48 @@ async def copy_recursive(self, src_path: str, dst_path: str) -> None:
                         os.unlink(local_tmp)
 
 
+    async def create_policy(
+        self,
+        policy_name: str,
+        path: str,
+        subject_cn: str,
+        privileges: list[str],
+    ) -> None:
+        """Create or replace an HDLF allow policy via the Policies API (idempotent PUT).
+
+        Grants the certificate with the given CN access to a specific path. The
+        Policies API lives at /policies/v1/ — a separate URL prefix from the
+        WebHDFS /webhdfs/v1/ prefix.
+
+        Args:
+            policy_name: Unique policy identifier, e.g. "fl-inspection-<uuid>".
+            path: HDLF path the policy applies to, e.g. "/<uuid>/". Must end
+                with "/" to cover the folder and its contents.
+            subject_cn: CN from the client certificate that should be granted
+                access, e.g. "<inspection_uuid>". Rendered as "x509:CN=<cn>".
+            privileges: HDLF privilege strings. Use ["browse", "open"] for
+                read-only access (browse = list directory; open = read file).
+                Handler result writes also need create, append, rename, and
+                delete for the atomic .tmp + delete + rename flow.
+        """
+        if self._session is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("HdlfClient must be used as an async context manager")
+        body = json.dumps(
+            {
+                "name": policy_name,
+                "type": "allow",
+                "resources": [f"path:{path}"],
+                "subjects": [f"x509:CN={subject_cn}"],
+                "privileges": privileges,
+            }
+        ).encode()
+        url = f"/policies/v1/{policy_name}"
+        status, _, response_body = await self._request("PUT", url, body=body, content_type="application/json")
+        if not (200 <= status < 300):
+            raise IOError(f"HDLF policy PUT {policy_name!r} returned HTTP {status}: {response_body[:200]!r}")
+        log.info("HDLF policy created", policy_name=policy_name, path=path, subject_cn=subject_cn)
+
+

 """FastAPI dependencies for the hdlf_server (Handler SDK API).
 
-A single `HdlfClient` is opened at app startup and shared across requests.
-HdlfClient owns one aiohttp ClientSession; sharing it across requests is
-the normal aiohttp pattern (per-request sessions would defeat connection
-pooling and multiply the mTLS handshake cost).
-
-The same lifespan also opens an :class:`InspectionResultsRepository` over
-the shared client (write endpoints live in ``handler_results_router.py``).
-Reusing the client means one mTLS handshake and one connection pool serve
-both the read endpoints (via ``InspectionReader``) and the write endpoint
-(via the repository).
+The app opens one `HdlfClient` at startup for readiness checks. Read/write
+requests do not use that process identity: handlers pass their own HDLF
+connection details in HTTP headers, and the request dependencies below build a
+short-lived client from those headers so HDLF sees the concrete handler's mTLS
+identity.
 
 Singleton storage uses ``app.state`` rather than module-level globals so
 that two FastAPI apps in the same process (a real one plus a test app,
 multi-tenant test runs) cannot trample each other. Tests that need to
-substitute the reader/client/repository should use
-``app.dependency_overrides``.
+substitute the reader/client/repository should use ``app.dependency_overrides``.
 """

@@ -134,6 +145,61 @@ def get_inspection_results_repository(request: Request) -> InspectionResultsRepo
     return repo
 
 
+def get_hdlf_connection_params(request: Request) -> HdlfConnectionParams:
+    """Build HDLF connection parameters from the handler-supplied headers.
+
+    The header values are request credentials, not authentication for this
+    service. They are forwarded into the WebHDFS mTLS client so HDLF reads and
+    writes happen as the concrete handler identity that called hdlf_server.
+    """
+    missing = [name for name in _HDLF_CREDENTIAL_HEADERS if not request.headers.get(name)]
+    if missing:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Missing HDLF credential headers: {', '.join(missing)}")
+
+    return HdlfConnectionParams(
+        rest_api_host=request.headers[HDLF_REST_API_HOST_HEADER],
+        container_id=request.headers[HDLF_CONTAINER_ID_HEADER],
+        client_certificate=SecretStr(request.headers[HDLF_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_HEADER]),
+        client_key=SecretStr(request.headers[HDLF_CLIENT_KEY_HEADER]),
+    )
+
+
+def _raise_bad_hdlf_credentials(exc: Exception) -> NoReturn:
+    """Translate malformed request HDLF credentials without exposing their values."""
+    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid HDLF credential headers") from exc
+
+
+async def get_request_reader(
+    params: HdlfConnectionParams = Depends(get_hdlf_connection_params),
+) -> AsyncIterator[InspectionReader]:
+    """Yield an ``InspectionReader`` authenticated with request credentials."""
+    async with AsyncExitStack() as exit_stack:
+        try:
+            reader = InspectionReader.from_params(params)
+            await exit_stack.enter_async_context(reader)
+        except (HdlfConfigurationError, ValueError, ssl.SSLError) as exc:
+            _raise_bad_hdlf_credentials(exc)
+        yield reader
+
+
+async def get_request_inspection_results_repository(
+    params: HdlfConnectionParams = Depends(get_hdlf_connection_params),
+) -> AsyncIterator[InspectionResultsRepository]:
+    """Yield a write repository authenticated with request credentials."""
+    async with AsyncExitStack() as exit_stack:
+        try:
+            repository = make_inspection_results_repository(params)
+            await exit_stack.enter_async_context(repository)
+        except (
+            HdlfConfigurationError,
+            InspectionResultsConfigurationError,
+            ValueError,
+            ssl.SSLError,
+        ) as exc:
+            _raise_bad_hdlf_credentials(exc)
+        yield repository
+
+

+def _secret_env_refs(job) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str]]:
+    """Return container env vars sourced from Secret keys as name→(secret, key)."""
+    refs = {}
+    for env_var in job.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env:
+        if not env_var.value_from or not env_var.value_from.secret_key_ref:
+            continue
+        secret_key_ref = env_var.value_from.secret_key_ref
+        refs[env_var.name] = (secret_key_ref.name, secret_key_ref.key)
+    return refs
+

diff --git a/tests/execution_engine/test_hdlf_cert_provisioner.py b/tests/execution_engine/test_hdlf_cert_provisioner.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..63a9ff0f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/execution_engine/test_hdlf_cert_provisioner.py
@@ -0,0 +1,125 @@
+"""Tests for per-inspection HDLF certificate provisioning."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock
+
+import pytest
+from pydantic import SecretStr
+from temporalio.exceptions import ApplicationError
+
+from fl_control_plane.execution_engine import hdlf_cert_provisioner
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_provision_inspection_access_grants_read_write_policy(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    """Per-inspection handler certs can read inputs and write handler results."""
+
+    class _FakeHdlfClient:
+        instances: list["_FakeHdlfClient"] = []
+
+        def __init__(self, *_args: object, **kwargs: object) -> None:
+            self.create_policy = AsyncMock()
+            self.put_object = AsyncMock()
+            self.exists = AsyncMock(return_value=True)
+            self.get_object = AsyncMock(return_value=hdlf_cert_provisioner._ACCESS_PROBE_BYTES)
+            self.delete_object = AsyncMock()
+            self.kwargs = kwargs
+            self.instances.append(self)
+
+        async def __aenter__(self) -> "_FakeHdlfClient":
+            return self
+
+        async def __aexit__(self, *_args: object) -> None:
+            return None
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(hdlf_cert_provisioner, "HdlfClient", _FakeHdlfClient)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        hdlf_cert_provisioner,
+        "get_settings",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(
+            hdlf_ca_issuer_name="pipeline-fl-hdlf-ca-issuer",
+            namespace="test-depl-name",
+            hdlf_inspection_cert_duration_hours=6,
+            hdlf_access_poll_timeout_seconds=1,
+            hdlf_access_poll_interval_seconds=0,
+        ),
+    )
+    issue_cert = AsyncMock(return_value="fl-job-exec-1-hdlf-cert")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(hdlf_cert_provisioner, "issue_inspection_cert", issue_cert)
+    read_secret = AsyncMock(return_value=(SecretStr("cert"), SecretStr("key")))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(hdlf_cert_provisioner, "_read_tls_secret", read_secret)
+
+    secret_name = await hdlf_cert_provisioner.provision_inspection_access("insp-1", "exec-1")
+
+    assert secret_name == "fl-job-exec-1-hdlf-cert"
+    _FakeHdlfClient.instances[0].create_policy.assert_awaited_once_with(
+        policy_name="fl-inspection-insp-1",
+        path="/insp-1/",
+        subject_cn="insp-1",
+        privileges=["browse", "open", "create", "append", "rename", "delete"],
+    )
+    issue_cert.assert_awaited_once_with(
+        inspection_id="insp-1",
+        execution_id="exec-1",
+        issuer_name="pipeline-fl-hdlf-ca-issuer",
+        namespace="test-depl-name",
+        duration_hours=6,
+    )
+    read_secret.assert_awaited_once_with("fl-job-exec-1-hdlf-cert", "test-depl-name")
+    assert len(_FakeHdlfClient.instances) == 2
+    _assert_access_probe(_FakeHdlfClient.instances[0], "insp-1")
+    _assert_access_probe(_FakeHdlfClient.instances[1], "insp-1")
+    assert _FakeHdlfClient.instances[1].kwargs["client_certificate"].get_secret_value() == "cert"
+    assert _FakeHdlfClient.instances[1].kwargs["client_key"].get_secret_value() == "key"
+
+
+def _assert_access_probe(fake_client: object, inspection_id: str) -> None:
+    """Assert the HDLF readiness probe writes, stats, reads, and deletes a temp file."""
+    put_call = fake_client.put_object.await_args  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    assert put_call is not None
+    probe_path = put_call.args[0]
+    assert probe_path.startswith(f"{inspection_id}/.fl-access-probe-")
+    assert put_call.args[1] == hdlf_cert_provisioner._ACCESS_PROBE_BYTES
+    assert put_call.kwargs == {"overwrite": True}
+    fake_client.exists.assert_awaited_once_with(probe_path)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    fake_client.get_object.assert_awaited_once_with(probe_path)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    fake_client.delete_object.assert_awaited_once_with(probe_path)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_probe_hdlf_inspection_access_deletes_probe_when_read_fails() -> None:
+    """The readiness probe cleans up its temp file when read-back fails."""
+    fake_client = SimpleNamespace(
+        put_object=AsyncMock(),
+        exists=AsyncMock(return_value=True),
+        get_object=AsyncMock(side_effect=IOError("OPEN returned HTTP 403")),
+        delete_object=AsyncMock(),
+    )
+
+    with pytest.raises(IOError, match="OPEN returned HTTP 403"):
+        await hdlf_cert_provisioner._probe_hdlf_inspection_access(  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+            fake_client,
+            "insp-1/.fl-access-probe-test",
+        )
+
+    probe_path = fake_client.put_object.await_args.args[0]
+    fake_client.delete_object.assert_awaited_once_with(probe_path)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_provision_inspection_access_fails_when_issuer_is_unset(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    """Without an issuer, per-inspection HDLF access fails as misconfiguration."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        hdlf_cert_provisioner,
+        "get_settings",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(hdlf_ca_issuer_name=""),
+    )
+
+    with pytest.raises(ApplicationError) as error_info:
+        await hdlf_cert_provisioner.provision_inspection_access("insp-1", "exec-1")
+
+    assert error_info.value.type == "ConfigError"
+    assert error_info.value.non_retryable is True
+    assert "EE_HDLF_CA_ISSUER_NAME" in str(error_info.value)

diff --git a/tests/hdlf_server/test_dependencies.py b/tests/hdlf_server/test_dependencies.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..7e1180f2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/hdlf_server/test_dependencies.py
@@ -0,0 +1,143 @@
+"""Unit tests for hdlf_server FastAPI dependencies."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+from fastapi import HTTPException
+from pydantic import SecretStr
+
+from fl_control_plane.inspection_results_repository import InspectionResultsConfigurationError
+from fl_shared.hdlf_client import HdlfConnectionParams
+from hdlf_server import dependencies
+
+
+def _params() -> HdlfConnectionParams:
+    """Build request-scoped HDLF params with dummy inline credentials."""
+    return HdlfConnectionParams(
+        rest_api_host="test.invalid",
+        container_id="test-container",
+        client_certificate=SecretStr("certificate"),
+        client_key=SecretStr("key"),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_request_reader_translates_context_entry_errors(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    """Reader context-entry credential errors surface as 400 responses."""
+
+    class BrokenReader:
+        """Reader stand-in whose session open fails like a malformed host would."""
+
+        @classmethod
+        def from_params(cls, _params: HdlfConnectionParams) -> "BrokenReader":
+            """Build the fake reader from request parameters."""
+            return cls()
+
+        async def __aenter__(self) -> "BrokenReader":
+            raise ValueError("bad base URL")
+
+        async def __aexit__(self, *args: object) -> None:
+            pass
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dependencies, "InspectionReader", BrokenReader)
+
+    dependency = dependencies.get_request_reader(_params())
+
+    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc_info:
+        await anext(dependency)
+
+    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 400
+    assert exc_info.value.detail == "Invalid HDLF credential headers"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_request_reader_preserves_endpoint_value_errors(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    """Reader dependency does not rewrite endpoint-side ValueError exceptions."""
+
+    class Reader:
+        """Reader stand-in that records cleanup arguments."""
+
+        def __init__(self) -> None:
+            self.exit_args: tuple[Any, ...] | None = None
+
+        @classmethod
+        def from_params(cls, _params: HdlfConnectionParams) -> "Reader":
+            """Build the fake reader from request parameters."""
+            return cls()
+
+        async def __aenter__(self) -> "Reader":
+            return self
+
+        async def __aexit__(self, *args: object) -> None:
+            self.exit_args = args
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dependencies, "InspectionReader", Reader)
+
+    dependency = dependencies.get_request_reader(_params())
+    reader = await anext(dependency)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="endpoint bug"):
+        await dependency.athrow(ValueError("endpoint bug"))
+
+    assert reader.exit_args is not None
+    assert reader.exit_args[0] is ValueError
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_request_repository_translates_context_entry_errors(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    """Repository context-entry credential errors surface as 400 responses."""
+
+    class BrokenRepository:
+        """Repository stand-in whose session open fails before endpoint code runs."""
+
+        async def __aenter__(self) -> "BrokenRepository":
+            raise InspectionResultsConfigurationError("cert missing")
+
+        async def __aexit__(self, *args: object) -> None:
+            pass
+
+    def make_repository(_params: HdlfConnectionParams) -> BrokenRepository:
+        return BrokenRepository()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dependencies, "make_inspection_results_repository", make_repository)
+
+    dependency = dependencies.get_request_inspection_results_repository(_params())
+
+    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc_info:
+        await anext(dependency)
+
+    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 400
+    assert exc_info.value.detail == "Invalid HDLF credential headers"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_request_repository_preserves_endpoint_configuration_errors(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+    """Repository dependency does not rewrite write-path configuration errors."""
+
+    class Repository:
+        """Repository stand-in that records cleanup arguments."""
+
+        def __init__(self) -> None:
+            self.exit_args: tuple[Any, ...] | None = None
+
+        async def __aenter__(self) -> "Repository":
+            return self
+
+        async def __aexit__(self, *args: object) -> None:
+            self.exit_args = args
+
+    def make_repository(_params: HdlfConnectionParams) -> Repository:
+        return Repository()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(dependencies, "make_inspection_results_repository", make_repository)
+
+    dependency = dependencies.get_request_inspection_results_repository(_params())
+    repository = await anext(dependency)
+
+    with pytest.raises(InspectionResultsConfigurationError, match="backend broke"):
+        await dependency.athrow(InspectionResultsConfigurationError("backend broke"))
+
+    assert repository.exit_args is not None
+    assert repository.exit_args[0] is InspectionResultsConfigurationError
